These include the class of women adorned with skirts and hairpins, as well as various types of solitary spirits.
We invoke them all with one mind: those who were beggars suffering from hunger and cold; prisoners executed by the state; those who perished in water or fire;

those who lost their lives to tigers and wolves; those who hanged themselves or took poison; those whose vengeful resentment has lingered for a thousand years; and those struck by lightning or buried under collapsing cliffs—a single point of spirit.
The startled spirits tremble with fear. (Alas! In the evening rain and blue smoke, cold magpies shriek; in the autumn wind and yellow leaves, crows fly in disorder.
Such is the state of those who have met with untimely death, this class of solitary ghosts and the like.
With single-minded devotion, I invoke all beings within the Dharma-realm and the six realms of existence, all sentient beings encompassed by the great earth, and the hosts of *pūtana* spirits—
those of countless varieties who dwell upon grasses and trees, the *chi-mei* and *wang-liang* demons, and the lingering souls and orphaned spirits of those deceased among both ourselves and others.
May our family members, relatives, and all the assembly,
relying on the power of the Triple Gem and depending upon secret mantras, come this very night at this moment to receive the unobstructed dharma-food of ambrosia.
Having received this unobstructed dharma-food of ambrosia...
The invocations above have been completed, and all have now arrived. May the great assembly, out of compassion, join their voices in lamentation:

"From recent times to the former dynasties, there were emperors and sovereigns of honored and majestic rank; meritorious relatives, kings, and dukes of noble lineage with jade leaves and golden branches;
ministers, high officials, ladies of the inner court, and classes of concubines and consorts—all have severed their dreams of the realm of Huaxu and come here to receive the flavor of the ambrosia."
A statesman among the court ministers, who had woven the threads of governance to rectify the age and shepherd the common people, failed to fulfill his loyal and virtuous aspirations.
Having lost favor and harboring sorrow, he was banished to a frontier land; yet with his soul lingering in longing for his country, he has now come to receive the flavor of the ambrosial Dharma.
Generals and martial ministers, commanding three armies, drew up battle arrays and clashed in combat; the sound of gongs and drums roared through heaven and earth.

Fighting in the north and campaigning in the south, they perished upon the desert fields. Having sacrificed their bodies for the sake of the nation, they now come to receive the flavor of the nectar of immortality.

Studying the ancients and mastering the present, you were a scholar of embroidered prose and rhymed verse. Illuminating the snow and stealing its light, you applied yourself with bitter resolve within the cold window.
Yet your destiny was thwarted; your name did not appear upon the golden list. Now, as a soul dwelling in deep sorrow, come to receive the flavor of the sweet nectar.
Renouncing what is dear and bidding farewell to kin, he entered the gates of the Empty Gate early on. Seeking the Way and searching for a teacher, his sole purpose was to transcend birth and death.
As summer passed and winter came, he did not realize that impermanence had arrived. Only by reflecting inwardly and turning back the light of consciousness can one swiftly realize the stage of Bodhi.
Clad in feathered robes and wearing yellow caps, you have long since resolved to cultivate the truth. You refine elixirs and burn cinnabar, nourishing your nature and returning to the primal breath.

Through asceticism and the exhaustion of the spirit, you hope to ascend to the rank of an immortal. Do not cling to this discarded form; come instead to receive the flavor of the nectar of immortality.

Filial sons and worthy grandsons, men of righteousness, valor, loyalty, and goodness, as well as heroic women and chaste wives—regarding death as returning home, they uphold their integrity and sacrifice their bodies, leaving behind a heroic spirit for a thousand ages.
May their resolute souls come now to partake of the flavor of the sweet dew.
The female monastic stream dwells upon the ground of golden light; like phoenixes soaring through the void, they remain untainted by worldly affairs.

Having not yet realized the unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*), they wander through the cycle of empty birth and death. May these pure spirits come to receive the flavor of the nectar of immortality (*amṛta*).

Whether one studies geography and astronomy, the categories of medicine and yin-yang, divination by hexagrams and tortoise shells, physiognomy and astrology, or reports of auspiciousness and discussions of misfortune—none can avoid the arrival of impermanence.
Only by discarding the false and returning to the true can one come to partake of the flavor of the nectar of immortality.
Sedentary shopkeepers and traveling merchants, those engaged in various kinds of business, and those skilled in many arts who seek wealth and profit through trade—
may these people, who have left their wells and villages to die in foreign lands, come in their wandering dreams to receive the flavor of the nectar of immortality.
Those who have broken the law and suffered punishment, long confined in dark prisons; those who, burdened by debt, plotted for wealth and became like vengeful creditors;
those afflicted by swellings, poisons, and epidemics; and those who perished from cold or hunger—may they swiftly depart from the Yellow Springs and come to receive the flavor of nectar.

Mangled by carriage wheels, their bodies crushed under horses' hooves; struck down by collapsing walls or crumbling cliffs, or who have committed suicide by cutting their own throats or hanging from beams;
those swept away by water or fire, or burned, bitten by tigers, or wounded by snakes—may these solitary spirits of the nine untimely deaths come to receive the flavor of the nectar of immortality.
Those who eat blood and consume raw fur, born and raised in the lands of barbarians; those burdened by debt and labor, along with concubines, handmaidens, and slaves;
the mute, the blind, the deaf, and the physically disabled—those destitute and helpless souls suffering in torment come now to partake of the flavor of ambrosia.
They were disobedient toward their parents; they brought resentment upon Heaven and Earth; they slandered the Buddha and deceived the Sangha; they destroyed images and burned sutras and verses.
Their false views were deep-seated, and their bitter retribution was boundless. May these ten-evil, frantic souls come now to receive the flavor of the ambrosia.

The Great Gate of Giving is opened to deliver the ranks of orphaned spirits. For the ancestors and those who have passed before, for the classes of karmic enemies of the five clans, and for all within the eight difficulties and the three paths—may they all be equally transcended and saved.
Relying upon the compassionate light of the Buddha, come to receive the flavor of the ambrosia.

Amitābha Buddha, you have long held boundless vows. Beholding those who have lost their way, constantly drifting and drowning in the sea of suffering, you extend your hand to guide them, specifically launching the compassionate vessel to arrive here.
You universally deliver all sentient beings, so that together they may attend the assembly at the Lotus Pond.
Therefore, from the ocean-like assembly of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in the Lotus Pond,
I, by means of the great compassionate power of the Buddha, invoke all sentient beings of both the hidden and visible realms,
including the hungry ghosts who have suffered from hunger and thirst for kalpas; do not disobey the Buddha’s command, but descend here!
Next, form the mudrā for summoning hungry ghosts (with the left hand in the gesture of fearlessness, extend the palm straight forward with the fingers pointing outward;
the right hand is held in front with the fingers extended and slightly curved). Recite the mantra of summoning: [insert mantra].
Oṃ jaṭa-keśi-he svāhā. (This seal and mantra appear in the *Jvālāmukhī-yamari-mātṛ-tantra*.
One should visualize oneself as [the deity]...)
Within the Bodhisattva, one should visualize upon the moon-disc of the heart the red syllable *hrīḥ*,
together with the mudrā and the letters, emitting rays of light.
The light illuminates those sinners, who recite divine mantras as they follow the radiance and arrive before the practitioner. The assembly praises their virtue and offers them comfort.

Having reached the ritual site (maṇḍala), they circumambulate the Buddha three times, prostrate themselves in worship, and after completing the dedication of merit, they again pay homage to the holy assembly and withdraw to sit on one side, departing from the altar.
From the eastern gate to the southern gate dwell the hosts of hell-beings. From the southern gate to the southwest corner dwell the hosts of hungry ghosts.
From the southwest corner to the western gate dwell those of the animal realm. From the western gate to the northwest corner are the palaces of the human realm.
From the northwest corner to the northern gate dwell the asuras. From the northern gate to the eastern gate dwell the celestial sages.

Alternatively, if there is no mandala hall, one may arrange seats from top to bottom according to rank, with the superior above and the inferior below; it is also permissible for them to sit on double-layered seats (the colors and mudrās are as described in the *Kaifaluo* [Record of Opening and Closing]).
Once the invocation has been performed and they have all gathered like clouds, one should praise and console them with a mind of compassion, causing them to rejoice.
Thirsting with longing for the Dharma, welcome, O sons of the Buddhas!
Because you have previously formed superior karmic conditions, you now encounter this auspicious assembly; do not give rise to anxiety or fear.
With single-minded thirst for the Dharma, do not let this moment pass. Let the precepts permeate your very being, and they shall swiftly cause you to leave the realms of suffering behind.
"You, all you sons of the Buddha, having encountered this place of enlightenment, shall have all your sins summoned into the vajra-palm.

Next, bind the seal for summoning sins (with both hands in vajra-bond, extend the *anāmikā* [ring fingers] like needles, and curve the *tarjanī* [index fingers] inward like hooks). The mantra for summoning sins is as follows: (The mantra for summoning sins:)
Oṃ sarvabuddhasamājādhiṣṭhānasattvasamaya hūṃ jaḥ. (The mudrā and mantra may be understood as follows:
one should visualize the syllable Hrīḥ, white in color, upon the tips of the two middle fingers.)
The syllable emits light and enters into that body; its emerging transgressions are like smoke and mist merging together. Question: Transgressions have no substantial reality.
Why, then, is it said now that they emerge like that smoke and mist as if they possessed substantial reality? Answer:
Although there is no substantial entity capable of filling heaven and earth or obstructing the eyes and mind such that one cannot perceive the pure realm of all Buddhas, now...

Borrowing the various mists as the objective sign (*ālambana-nimitta*), one summons the transgressions. As stated in the *Vajra-ākarṣaṇī-sūtra*: "The crookedness of the power of progress is overcome by patience and vows;
all assume the form and attire of Vajrapāṇi, ensuring they do not touch one another. One visualizes oneself as the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Upon the moon-disc of the heart, one contemplates a white syllable Hrīḥ, from which issue hook-like flames of light. From the mouth, the secret [mantra] issues forth.
The mantra hooks and gathers all sentient beings’ karma of the three evil destinies, as well as one’s own karma of the three evil destinies.
These appear black like clouds and mist; all the sins are summoned into the palm and transformed into the forms of various spirits.
As stated in the *Vajraśekhara-yoga-pāṭha*: "When reciting this secret [mantra], visualize those sinful forms as spirits, black in color with hair standing on end. Then, with both...

The fingers of the various [hands] are each hooked together, with the tips inserted into the palms. Visualize that by means of the two fingers of the *jinri* (advancing power), the transgression is hooked and clamped, causing it to enter the palm.

Following this, perform the mudrā for crushing transgressions: the remaining fingers are pressed against one another face-to-face, while the *nin-nan* (patience and vow) fingers are extended straight like needles.
All evil karmas and sins are destroyed, Just as the fires at the end of an eon are extinguished;
When the fire is extinguished, they are reduced to vajra-dust.
Next, bind the mudrā for destroying sins.
Oṃ vajrapāṇi-mūṣṭi-puthaje sarvāpad-bhañjana-nipramuktake sarvāpada-gati-vyāghāte sarvasattvānāṃ sarvārtha-kāra-vajre.
(Combined) *Samaya hūṃ traṭ*.
(The mudrā and mantra of the Master may be understood as follows:
At the tips of the two middle fingers, visualize *traṭ* on the left.)
The syllable RA (repha). Visualize the syllable ṬHA on the right, both golden in color.
At this point, the practitioner’s own body increases in size.
Visualize the body of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva as being blue and green. With each recitation of the mantra once, rub and shake the two middle fingers.
Upon the final recitation, cross the hands, clap them to make a sound, and imagine that mountain of sins collapsing like a fallen tile roof.
As for the previously summoned sins that were like smoke and mist, they shall disperse instantly upon this thought. Question: Sins have no inherent substance or characteristics.
How is it crushed? Answer: It is precisely because it is non-existent that it is said to be crushed. If it were determinately existent, how could it be crushed?
(The *Gouzui jing* says: "Visualize the syllable HŪṂ in blue upon the lunar disc of the mind, from which light radiates forth...")
Regarding the signs of prior karmic offenses, one should strike three times with the *mudrā* of the *kṣānti-pāramitā* (patience) to destroy the forms of those accumulated sins.
Reciting the secret mantra (*mantra*), the signs of sin are completely destroyed and eliminated without remainder. The *Vajraśekhara-bhāvanā-vidhi* states:
"Visualize the syllable *ḍha* at the tip of the *praṇidhāna-pāramitā* (vow), and visualize the syllable *ṭha* at the tip of the *kṣānti-pāramitā*. Furthermore, above these syllables, visualize..."

A flame arises. Taking hold of that sinner with both hands, recite the mantra for destroying sins. Having recited the secret words, rub [the ashes] vigorously using the method of snapping the fingers:
the right hand above and the left hand below. Alternatively, according to the *Vajraśekhara-sūtra*, form the Trailokyavijaya mudrā with the body and visualize a single-pronged vajra;
recite the mantra with a fierce voice, clapping the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhāna* fingers three times. As stated in the text: "Regarding karmic retribution..."
Second: Within karma, there is further the accomplishment of both manifest activity and seeds. Among manifest karmas, there are those that are determinate and those that are indeterminate.
In this present seal, it is the indeterminate karma that is extinguished.
Fixed karma cannot be altered; by the power of samādhi empowerment, all obstacles and difficulties from beginningless time are entirely extinguished.

Next, bind the seal for destroying fixed karma (with both hands in the vajra-palms, bend the second joints of the index fingers, and press the two thumbs against the two ring fingers). The mantra for purifying karma is as follows: [Mantra]
Oṃ vajrakarma-cuḍāmaṇi-sarvārthasādhani-buddhasatye namaḥ samaya hūṃ. (The mudrā and mantra may be understood accordingly.
Above the moon-disc of the heart, one should visualize a blue syllable Hrīḥ emerging.)
The light illuminates the various hosts of spirits before you.
Regarding all karmic obstructions that prevent one from encountering the appearance of Buddhas in the world or from performing repentance, one should contemplate their intrinsic purity.
One should fundamentally not form conceptualizations of action.
Contemplate those hosts of spirits, the Buddha, and the mind as being without distinction among the three;
this is called "shattering determinate karma. This...
This single dharma is precisely for severing the cognitive obscurations;
students must know this. (This seal-mantra appears in the *Acala-mūla-tantra*. There are twelve kinds of seals for the confession of fixed karma that are not common to all Buddhas.
Furthermore, it says: "Form the seal of fixed karma with the hands. Visualize oneself as the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, upon whose heart-moon disc [is the seed syllable]. )

Visualize the blue syllable *Hrīḥ* emitting light. Recite the secret mantra mentally, illuminating all the aforementioned spirits and the karmic obstructions that have not been purified through confession by the Buddhas, as well as the karma of the three evil destinies pertaining to oneself. This transforms heavy karma into light;
"heavy" refers here to determinate (*niyata*) karma. Since this practice transforms and extinguishes such coarse and heavy determinate karma, employ the two seals mentioned above.

The purification of manifest conduct is complete. The subtle seeds are eliminated by the Seal that Eradicates Transgressions (*āpatti-mudrā-vināśana*). Purifying karma follows the ritual manual (*vidhi-sūtra*).
The nature of transgression is fundamentally empty, yet it is created by the mind.
When the mind ceases, the transgression also perishes. When the transgression perishes and the mind ceases, both are empty; this is what is called true repentance (*pratideśanā*).
Next, form the mudrā for repentance and the eradication of sins (with the two hands in vajra-bond, bend the second joints of the thumbs, and press the ring fingers with the middle fingers;
the mantra for repentance is as follows).
Oṃ sarvabuddhapūjā-pratihatā-jayā svāhā. (The mudrā and mantra may be understood accordingly; one should visualize:)
Above the two bent fingers,
there is a white syllable *hrīḥ*. It enters the body of that ghost,
like the sun scorching dew.
Its appearance is such that the stains of transgression melt away like ink, flowing down from the feet and soaking into the earth until it reaches the adamantine base (*vajratala*). Question:

Since they have already been summoned, subdued, and shattered previously, why perform repentance again now? Answer: Those previous instances were all repentance at the level of principle (*li-xuanchan*); now...

This is precisely what constitutes repentance for these matters; because principle and phenomena are unimpeded (*li-shi wu-ai*), there is no confusion between them. Furthermore, it was asked: "What kind of offense is like ink? The answer is:
"An offense is black karma (*kṛṣṇa-karman*); therefore, it is represented by 'black. As for 'ink' (*zhì*), it carries the sense of flowing or streaming forth; hence it is said to be 'like ink.'"
O sons of the Buddhas, having already performed repentance, the sins accumulated over a hundred kalpas are instantaneously and completely eliminated in a single thought-moment;
like fire consuming dry grass, they are extinguished utterly without remainder.
A single drop of cool water can eliminate hunger, thirst, and fever; by sprinkling it upon the gate of the crown, it causes all to attain peace and happiness.
Next, form the *Amṛta-dāna-mudrā* (or the *Śītala-dāna-mudrā*) of the Tathāgata of Wondrous Form with the right hand’s webbed fingers...
Rotate the wrist forward; advance the fingers of the *dhyāna-mudrā* and snap them together while reciting the Amṛta-mantra:
*Namo surupaye dhartadhāye tatte taṃ oṃ suru suru prasu ru prasu ru svāhā.*
(The Master’s seal-mantra may be understood as follows.
While forming the mudrā and reciting the mantra, one should visualize that upon the left hand there is a white syllable *vaṃ*. From it flows forth nectar...)
The dew is like water, silver in color, and formed by true wisdom.
Taking it with the right hand, one sprinkles it into the void,
visualizing all devas, humans, and ghosts.

Those of similar kind who touch this nectar all become endowed with physical form; fierce fires are entirely extinguished, and they universally attain refreshing coolness, free from the perception of hunger and thirst, as the obstructions of mental grasping are extinguished.
"From immeasurable kalpas past, you have created various evil karmas and given rise to stinginess and greed;
by the power of this karma, your throats were closed. By means of this secret mantra, may they all be opened and made passable.

Next, perform the seal for opening the throat (*kaṇṭhavivaraṇa-mudrā*). (The *Kalparāja-sūtra* states: "Visualize holding a lotus with the left hand; with the right hand, [perform] the *kṣānti-dhyāna* [gesture] and snap the fingers to make a sound, while reciting accordingly...")
To open the throat by playing [the instrument], the mantra is as follows:
Oṃ namo bhagavate ārya-avalokiteśvarāya tathāgatāya (The mudrā and mantra may be understood accordingly.
Form the mudrā and recite the mantra. Visualize a blue lotus flower within the palm of the left hand.)
Visualize a white letter *A* upon the flower, from which flows the water of intrinsic nature (*dharmatā*), exceedingly pure and cool.

Taking some with the right hand, sprinkle it into the void. Visualize that all the hosts of spirits, upon touching this water, have their throats become vast, cool, moist, and free from all obstruction.
Question: Why were the *hrīḥ* (dvi-svāra) syllables used extensively previously, while here they are used alone?
[Question]: What is this "syllable" (*akṣara*)? [Answer]: The syllable *a* is the seed of speech; therefore, it is continued in use based on the three original texts.
(This is the throat-opening mudrā of the Samantabhadra Tathāgata. It is according to the explanation of the Dharma Master Citri;
that master was a Bodhisattva of the stage of application (*prayogamārga*). One should visualize it within one's own body.)
The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, upon the moon-disc of his heart,
visualizes the white syllable Hrīḥ emitting light that illuminates the aforementioned spirits and others; with his hands he forms the mudrā.
Seal with the Coolness-bestowing Mudrā; recite the secret mantra mentally while performing the patience and dhyāna mudrās and opening the lotus of the left hand.
At that time, visualize that the throats of the spirits and other beings open of their own accord, becoming permeable.
Upon attaining unimpededness, one is able to produce sound and receive the name.
According to the *Suwenji* (Record of Following What is Heard), when practicing the meditation of the right hand, one should visualize a lunar disc.
Upon the disc, visualize a white letter A, from which flows the Dharma-water of the nectar of Prajñā. When striking with the hand of patience during meditation, the left hand is like a lotus.
The flowers open and unfold; nectar fills their centers. Visualize that the throats of all ghosts and spirits are opened and unobstructed, becoming cool, refreshing, and moistened.

"Speak, O sons of the Buddha! Now that I have performed the seal-mantra for you, your throats shall open of their own accord; you shall attain unimpeded penetration and be freed from all obstacles and difficulties."
O sons of the Buddha, I now extol for you the auspicious name of the Tathāgata,
which shall enable you to forever leave behind the sufferings of the three miserable realms and the eight difficulties, and to always be true and pure sons of the Tathāgata.

Namo Ratnaśrī Tathāgata. (With both hands in the vajra-palms mudrā: the fingers of the six perfections are crossed inwardly; the tips of the thumbs meet at the center of the chest; the two thumbs of the dhyāna fingers form vajra-palms; the fingers of the six perfections are crossed inwardly; the tips of the thumbs meet at the center of the chest;

the dhyāna and wisdom fingers are held upright on their sides). By praising the Seven Buddhas, one obtains two benefits: first, one is able to universally eliminate all karmic retribution and obstacles; second, one adorns oneself and others, enabling them to become vessels of the Dharma.
Namo ratnatrayāya dharmadhātve (Recite that Tathāgata’s name and form his mudrā;
one should not depart from the visualization of him as inseparable from oneself.)
O sons of the Buddha,
if you hear the name of the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava, it will cause all the fires of your afflictions and karmic deeds to be completely extinguished.

Homage to the Tathāgata Vigatabhaya (Right hand held upright at the chest; the *kṣānti*, *dhyāna*, and *jñāna* fingers are joined; the palm is turned downward with the fingers hanging down; the left palm is turned upward and extended).
Homage to the Tathāgata Vigatādveṣanayaṭaptaghaṭa.
O sons of the Buddha, if you hear the name of this Tathāgata, it will enable you to always be free from fear.
May they attain peace and happiness, be forever free from fear and alarm,
and dwell in pure joy.
Homage to the Tathāgata Vipula-kāya!
Namo Bhagavate Vipaśyine Tathāgatāya Arhate Samyaksaṃbuddhāya.
O sons of the Buddha, if one hears the name of the Tathāgata Vipula-kāya, one will be able to...
May you hungry ghosts with needle-like throats have the fires of karma cease their burning, attain refreshing clarity,
and find sweetness in whatever food and drink you receive.
The Flavor of Dew.
Homage to the Tathāgata Subhavarṇa. Namo surūpāya tathāgatāya.
O sons of the Buddha, if you hear the name of the Tathāgata Sublime Form Body,
it shall cause you all to never again experience ugliness, and your sense faculties will be complete.
His feet were complete; his marks and signs were perfectly fulfilled,
most excellent and majestic, being the foremost in both the heavens and the human realm.
Namo to the Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna (join both hands empty at the chest in the lotus gesture).
Namo to the Buddhas, the Sons of the Victors, beginning with Vajradatta.
If you hear the name of the Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna, it shall cause you all to be fully endowed with wealth and treasures.
Whatever one requires shall be obtained according to one's wishes; its enjoyment shall be inexhaustible.
Homage to the Tathāgata Amitābha (with the right hand pressing down upon the left, the *dhyāna* and *jñāna* fingers touching).
Namo Amitābhāya Tathāgatāya.
"O Kātyāyana and all you sons of the Buddha, if you hear the name of the Tathāgata Amitābha,
it will enable you to go [to his land]."
May they be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss, arise by transformation from a lotus flower,
and enter the stage of non-retrogression.
Homage to the Tathāgata Vast and Great Majestic Virtue Sovereign Radiance of the World.
Namo lokavidveṣiṇe nātidīpta-rabhasa-tapta-gataye. (Right hand: fist with the ring finger extended upward;
snap the ring finger against the middle finger.
Left hand: palm facing upward, all five fingers extended.)

O sons of the Buddha: if you hear the name of the Tathāgata Vast and Majestic Power, Sovereign Radiance, it will enable you to obtain five kinds of merit. First, you shall be the most preeminent among all in the world;
second, you shall obtain a Bodhisattva body that is dignified and majestic.
Third, its majestic power is vast and great,
surpassing all non-Buddhists and celestial Māras,
like the sun illuminating the world and manifesting over the great ocean.
The merit is most sublime. Fourth, one attains great mastery;
whatever one directs toward is as one wishes, like a bird flying through the sky without obstruction. Fifth, ...
One attains great firmness, the radiance of wisdom, and a body and mind as transparent and clear as a lapis lazuli bead.
(Having finished the praise, the Ācārya says:)

O Sons of the Buddha: these seven Tathāgatas, by the power of their vows, rescue sentient beings, causing them to forever leave behind afflictions and escape the sufferings of the three miserable realms, attaining peace, security, and eternal bliss.
By reciting even once their names, one shall be free from suffering for a thousand lifetimes and realize the Unsurpassed Way.
(Recite three times.)
Next, I take refuge in the Triple Gem with you all:
I take refuge in the Buddha, the Honored One among two-legged beings; I take refuge in the Dharma, the Honored One free from desire;
I take refuge in the Saṅgha, the Honored One among assemblies. By taking refuge in the Buddha, one does not fall into hell.
By taking refuge in the Dharma, one does not fall among the hungry ghosts; by taking refuge in the Saṅgha, one does not fall among the animals.

O children of the Buddha, you have completed your refuge in the Buddha, your refuge in the Dharma, and your refuge in the Saṅgha. (The foregoing is recited three times by the Ācārya as a formal declaration.)
Because of taking refuge in the Triple Gem,
one firmly upholds the Dharma according to the teachings; having departed from the path of false views,
I therefore pay homage with a sincere heart.

Next, form the Seal of the Triple Gem (with the left hand, make a fist and extend the index finger vertically at the chest; with the right hand, bend the index finger. Visualize while reciting the mantra).
Oṃ bākaṃ. Homage to the Buddha.
Homage to the Dharma. Homage to the Saṅgha.
I now resolve my mind, not for myself...
Those who seek the blessings and rewards of humans and devas, the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas,
and even the Bodhisattvas of the various stages of the provisional vehicles,
should rely solely upon the Supreme Vehicle to resolve their minds on Bodhi, vowing that they and all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm may simultaneously attain it together.

This mind of awakening now aroused for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* is far removed from all natures and characteristics, from the aggregates (*skandha*), bases (*āyatana*), and elements (*dhātu*), as well as from the grasping at subject and object.
All phenomena are entirely without self; they are equal like space. One's own mind is fundamentally unarisen, for its empty nature is perfectly quiescent.
Just as all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have generated the great bodhicitta, so too do I generate it. Therefore, I prostrate with a sincere heart.
Next, I shall cause you all to resolve upon Bodhicitta; listen attentively. (The Acarya strikes the wooden fish once and recites the Four Great Vows:
Sentient beings are boundless; I vow to deliver them all. Afflictions are inexhaustible; I vow to sever them all.
Dharma gates are immeasurable; I vow to study them all. The Buddha-way is unsurpassed; I vow to perfect it.
"Even if a wheel of red-hot iron were to spin upon the crown of your head, you must never, for the sake of such suffering,
abandon the bodhicitta. Next,
form the seal of generating the bodhicitta (join the two hands empty-palmed, like the shape of a lotus, and place the seal upon the heart).
Oṃ bodhicittam utpādayāmi. (The master’s mudrā and mantra may be understood as they are;
one should contemplate that the Buddha in one’s own mind, sentient beings, and [the Buddha]—these three—are without distinction.)
In a single thought-moment, it melts into one vast lunar disc,
like the moon on the night of the fifteenth day of the eighth month at midnight when the sky is cloudless. To the utmost...
It is profoundly cool and pure, equal to empty space. Within the lunar disc, visualize a golden letter *A*, as fine as the tip of an autumn hair;
because it is neither existent nor non-existent, at that moment one must not add anything to cognition.
Above, there is no Buddha to be realized; below, there are no beings to be delivered; in between, there are no practices to be cultivated. Thus, afflictions and bodhi [are one].
The complete purification of birth-and-death and nirvana—this is the essential point. You should apply your mind well to this.
Not only will it bring benefit to spirits and deities, but practitioners will also soon attain realization within this very state.
(After the Master has recited the mantra three times in unison with the assembly, he says:)
I have now brought you all to the full awakening of the bodhicitta. O sons of the Buddha, you should know that this bodhicitta arises from great compassion;
it is the direct cause for attaining Buddhahood, the root of wisdom, capable of destroying ignorance, afflictions, and evil karma, and remaining unstained and uncorrupted by them.
Next, I shall confer upon you the Samaya Precepts (the practitioner strikes the wooden fish once and says):

1. The Precept of Restraining Evil Conduct: there is no evil that is not severed; it gives rise to the practice of the Right Path and is the cause for the virtue of severance (*prahāṇa-guṇa*); through its cultivation, the Dharma-body (*dharmakāya*) is perfected.

2. The Precept of Gathering Wholesome Dharmas: there is no wholesome dharma that is not accumulated; it gives rise to the practice that assists the Path and is the cause for the virtue of wisdom (*jñāna-guṇa*); through its cultivation, [the Body of Bliss is perfected].

The Reward Body (*saṃbhogakāya*). Third is the precept of gathering sentient beings: there is no birth that is not saved; one gives rise to the non-abiding path, which is the cause of benevolent virtue.

Through cultivation, the Transformation Body (*nirmāṇakāya*) is perfected. (Once the great vessel is completed, it is capable of receiving the Jewel Precepts. Regarding the *samaya*, it follows the *Mahāsukhavajrasamādhi-sūtra*.)
It is said: Samādhi is called the "original vow" (samaya), and it is also called "time," "appointed agreement," and "maṇḍala.
These are alternative names; thus, there are four types: first, the Great [Maṇḍala]; second, the Samaya; third, the Dharma; and fourth, the Karma.
As for the maṇḍala, these four collectively encompass all maṇḍalas. Furthermore, the samaya is also the four wisdom-mudrās (jñānamudrā). That is to say:
The Great Wisdom Seal (*mahājñānamudrā*), the Samaya Wisdom Seal (*samayajñānamudrā*), the Dharma Wisdom Seal (*dharmajñānamudrā*), and the Karma Wisdom Seal (*karmajñānamudrā*).
Furthermore, the *Divyavyākhyāna* explains the meaning of *samaya* as follows: "Samaya" signifies equality, the original vow, the removal of obstacles, and the act of awakening.
Regarding "equality," it means that when the Tathāgata realizes this samādhi through direct perception, all sentient beings—regardless of their various [differences]..."
In body, speech, and mind, I am entirely equal to the Tathāgata. In meditative concentration and wisdom, I am also ultimately equal to the Body of Real Mark (*lakṣaṇa-kāya*).
From the first moment of generating the bodhicitta until the fulfillment of the stages (*bhūmi*) and the perfections (*pāramitā*), I am likewise ultimately equal.
Therefore, I utter these words of truth to address all sentient beings: "If what I have said is certainly not false, then it shall also accord with the assembly of all beings."
When one gives rise to these words of sincere truth, one also receives the empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of the three secrets; endowed with inexhaustible adornments, one becomes equal to the Tathāgata.
For this reason, one is able to perform vajra activities, and thus it is called *samaya*. Regarding the "original vow" (*pūrvapratijñā*):
when the Tathāgata realized this *samaya*, he saw that all sentient beings were already fully awakened as Buddhas.

For this reason, he immediately established a great vow: "From this day forth, through the Universal Gate and by means of immeasurable skillful expedients, I shall bring all sentient beings together so that they may all attain unsurpassed bodhi.
Until the realm of sentient beings is exhausted, my activities shall never cease. If there are sentient beings who follow my original vow and utter these words of sincere truth,"
It also causes all the activities performed by them to become entirely of the nature of vajra; therefore, it is called *samaya*.

Regarding the "removal of obstacles": the Tathāgata perceives that all sentient beings possess the Tathāgata-dharmadhātu, yet because they possess even a single thought of ignorance, [the dharmadhātu] is constantly before them and they fail to realize it. For this reason, he utters these words of truth: "I now vow..."
One should employ various skillful means for the sake of all sentient beings to remove the cataracts from their eyes.
If my vow is to be surely fulfilled, then when I speak these words of sincere truth according to my skillful means, may all sentient beings obtain the stainless eye;
because all obscurations and veils are utterly exhausted, it is called the *samaya*.
Regarding the meaning of "startling awakening": because all sentient beings are in the sleep of ignorance, they do not themselves realize or know such virtues;
therefore, [the Tathāgata] uses words of discourse to stir them, causing them to awaken.

He likewise startles and awakens the various bodhisattvas, causing them to emerge from the cave of meditative concentration (*dhyāna*) and train in the *siṃhavijṛmbhita-samādhi* (the lion’s yawn samādhi). If...
When practitioners of mantras proclaim this samaya, we Buddhas shall likewise remember and uphold our original vows and must not transgress them;
just as a king, having established his own laws, subsequently honors and follows them himself, it is therefore called *samaya*.
Because it possesses such vast, profound, and subtle meanings, it is named *samādhi*.
"Ye! You who have received the Buddha's precepts immediately enter the rank of all Buddhas. Having attained a status equal to the Greatly Awakened One, you are truly the sons of the Buddhas."
Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā (the two hands in the vajra-bind; extend the *tarjanī* and *anāmikā* fingers like needles).
Recite the mantra: Oṃ samayasattva vaṃ.
(The master’s mudrā and mantra are as previously explained. One should visualize the white syllable *vaṃ* within the mudrā, emitting great radiance that pervades everywhere.)

This light illuminates all sentient beings who have been invited. Those sentient beings, through the illumination of this light and the Three Times Buddhas, simultaneously fulfill the *śīla-pāramitā*.
Visualizing the wholesome dharmas of the *dharmadhātu* as light, its flowing radiance confers empowerment (*abhiṣeka*), which is stored within their bodies.
Their bodies become identical to Samantabhadra; sitting upon a great lunar disc, they succeed to the office of the Buddhas and become the legitimate sons of the Buddhas.
According to the meaning of this text, there is no separate visualization;
rather, one naturally accomplishes the reception of the confession just as with mudrās and mantras.
As stated in the *Vajraśekhara Sūtra*, if one recites...
Reciting this mantra once is like entering a maṇḍala circle and realizing samādhi;
all wholesome dharmas will be completely fulfilled, as will the threefold pure precepts.

Simultaneously perfected, his body becomes identical to that of Samantabhadra, seated upon a great lunar disc. All Buddhas, recollecting their former original vows, observe and protect him with mindfulness.
Even if there were someone who had previously received the Buddha’s precepts but, through an evil mind, violated and destroyed them so that they were no longer pure—
If one recites this mantra seven times, the defilements of transgressing the precepts will all be purified, and all categories of discipline will be restored as they were before.
Regarding all mandala rites, even if one has not yet received formal transmission from a master, it is permitted to perform them after reciting the mantra seven times.
[This does not constitute the offense of stealing].
Now, having completed the bestowal of the samaya precepts for you all, from this day forward, I shall enable you to enter the rank of the Tathāgata.
You are true sons of the Buddha, born through transformation from the Dharma, and have obtained a share of the Buddha-dharma.
"You sentient beings, both of the dark and the light realms— I now bestow upon you the food of nectar;
Through the empowerment of the Dharma, it pervades the ten directions, Causing each and every one of you to be fully satiated.
Next, bind the mudrā of the Tathāgata of Immeasurable Majestic Virtue, Sovereign Radiance (as the Tibetan text notes: visualize the left hand as the seal).

The commentary *Suīwénjì* states: "Regarding the character '持' (zhí), there is a basis for reading it as '如' (rú); this principle is highly appropriate. The practitioner should reflect upon this. (The character '持' is on the right wing; it denotes the practice of patience and dhyāna).
VAḤSARVA-THATHĀGATA-AJALUKATE VAṂ VARA VAṂ VARA SAṂVARA SAṂVARA HŪṂ.
(The mudrā and mantra for the attendant may be understood accordingly. The attendant takes [the vessel].)
Sprinkle water on the wrists and into the buckets.
Retire to your original positions. The Master should, with his right hand, snap his fingers in a threatening manner to dispel the Māras of the left hand.
Obstruction. Recite "HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ" three times.
Question: What kind of māras are there in the hands?
Answer: Because there are various *śi* worms within the hands.
Next, transform the visualization of emptiness by reciting "Oṃ Khaṃ" three times.
Question: What is the intention behind transforming this hand into emptiness? Answer:

Because this hand is composed of the two kinds of impurities—the red and the white—it is emptied so that it may become a hand adorned with supreme and wondrous merit. Question: Regarding what has come before...
When one enters meditative concentration (*dhyāna-samādhi*), one is oneself a bodhisattva; why then, at this time, do you again dispatch Māra to transform space? Answer:

The *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* states that after the World-Honored One had preached the *Anantārtha-sūtra*, he again entered samādhi and emitted light; later, when opening the precious stūpa, he again entered concentration and emitted light.
Is this not redundant? It is simply because a single matter manifests a single dharma, analogous to the worldly case where...
In the rites of ancestral temple worship, it is not that one does not undergo purification through fasting and bathing; yet, upon ascending the hall, one washes the hands once more.

Why? To manifest reverence. Now, by dispatching the transformation of the māras into emptiness once again, one manifests the depth of compassion and the extremity of pity—the intensity of the mind’s application.
Then, in a single thought-moment, one suddenly fashions sublime and wondrous hands; upon the palms...
From within [the heart], a red syllable *baṃ* emerges and transforms into a red lotus flower. Upon the flower, one visualizes a white syllable *vaṃ*.
From the bindu within it, inexhaustible food and drink flow forth.

One visualizes that the water vessels before one become entirely filled with Magadhan *droṇa* measures, adorned with the seven precious jewels and overflowing with sublime and excellent foods and so forth. Then, one visualizes this syllable.
From these seeds, inexhaustible food and drink flow forth, filling the entire *dharmadhātu*.
Recite the mantra *Oṃ āḥ hūṃ* one hundred and eight times, or forty-nine times, as you yourself shall know the proper time. Next, recite the mantra for transforming the food;
with each recitation, visualize taking the food and drink from within the *bindu* and sprinkling it into space.
(The corresponding version of the sutra states: Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying, "O Greatly Compassionate World-Honored One, I pray that you will deliver me from my suffering.
Why is this? Last night at the third watch, while walking in meditation in a quiet place, I was reflecting on the Dharma I had received when I saw a *yankou* ghost who spoke to me, saying:)"
"Three days from now, your life will surely come to an end, and you shall be reborn among the hungry ghosts. I asked the ghost, "How may I escape this suffering?

The hungry ghost replied, "If you can give alms to hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *nayutas* of hungry ghosts as numerous as the sands of the Ganges—those who are Brahmins, seers, officials under Yama, and the dark functionaries of the path of karma—"
To all the spirits, their attendants, and kinsmen, as well as those who have passed away long ago, food and drink are bestowed equally and universally upon the hungry ghosts (preta).
You shall obtain increased longevity. [The preta] addressed the World-Honored One, saying: "How can immeasurable food and drink be manifested so that they are sufficient?
The Buddha told Ānanda: "Do not fear now. I recall that in the past, during immeasurable kalpas, when I was once a brāhmaṇa..."

From the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, you shall receive a dhāraṇī named the "Dhāraṇī Method of the Tathāgata Immeasurable Majestic Virtue, Sovereignty, and Radiance. If you are well able to perform this dhāraṇī method...

Consecrate it seven times. This can cause a single meal to transform into various kinds of ambrosial food and drink, which is then able to fully satisfy all hungry ghosts, Brahmin sages, and diverse classes of spirits numbering as many as the sands of hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Ganges Rivers.
All these beings shall obtain exquisite and sublime food and drink until they are completely satiated. Each and every one of such a multitude shall thus attain *māṃsī*.
The *shu* used in the kingdom of Kāśmīra—this food and this water are equal in measure to the *dharmadhātu*.

By consuming them, they are inexhaustible, and all shall attain the fruits of sainthood and liberate themselves from bodies of suffering. The Buddha told Ānanda: "You should now receive this *dhāraṇī* method;
it shall cause your merit and longevity to increase, and cause hungry ghosts to be reborn in the heavens or in pure lands, receiving the bodies of humans and devas. It is able to...
This causes the donor to transform obstacles, eliminate calamities, prolong their years and increase their lifespan, attract supreme merit in the present life, and shall attain Bodhi, and so forth.
(Note: This mantra traditionally contains an extra character, "wán" [vaṃ]; it should be removed in accordance with the ritual procedures of the original scripture.)

"O sons of the Buddha, I have now performed the seal and mantra for you all. I shall transform this single meal into immeasurable food, as vast as Mount Sumeru and equal in measure to the Dharma-realm, such that it can never be exhausted."
By the power of this mantra, transform the food into an ocean of milk; universally bestow it upon the hungry ghosts and others so that their bodies and minds are all fully satiated.
Then, re-forming the previous mudrā, recite the Ocean of Milk mantra.
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ vaṃ*.
(The master’s mudrā and mantra may be understood from this.
One should visualize that nectar flows forth from within the *bindu*, and taking it with the right hand, one snaps the fingers.)
Sprinkling into space, it poured down like rain;
wherever it reached, it immediately became a great river of ghee and curd. Question:
How can a small amount of water from a tiny vessel fill the entire Dharma-realm?
Answer: It is because the power of the mind is inconceivable.

How much more so when it relies upon the power of divine mantras, the visualization of seed-syllables (*bīja*), and even the secret empowerment of all Buddhas and the power of meditative concentration (*dhyāna*). How could this be...?
It cannot transform the small into the great or change the few into the many.

For instance, if one were to take a single cup of wine and, through the power of skillful means, transform it into a drizzling rain, how much more so must this be the case for the inconceivable power of divine mantras?

Furthermore, the practitioner must not fail to apply their mind with focused concentration. Again, he asked: "For what reason do you not offer food and drink as alms, yet instead [use these mantras]?"
[The questioner] asked about the use of water. [The Buddha] replied: "Those in the realm of hungry ghosts (*preta*) are mostly scorched by the fires of their karma;

therefore, I now offer them water to douse and extinguish those karmic fires. The Buddha further said: "For hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas, those hungry ghosts have not even heard the names of drinks or water, let alone having been able to drink them.
He also said: "Those hungry ghosts stand on the banks of the Ganges yet do not see the water; even if they were to see it, it would transform [into pus or blood]."
It turns into pus and blood; when one drinks it, it enters the abdomen and transforms into fierce flames, burning the heart and belly with unbearable agony.
Alas! Alas! Therefore, I now bestow water upon them, intending this very purpose. Furthermore, the Tibetan version says *sru ba*, which means "water.
One thus knows that the original basis for the offering of food was the offering of water. Nowadays, worldly people do not understand this, and [the practice] has largely...
Even the practice of offering water with food has been lost; how much more so is the current practice of offering food? For one does not use water exclusively;
rather, one places seven grains of rice from within that vessel into the ten directions. Therefore, do not harbor doubts about these matters.
"O sons of the Buddha, I have now performed the seal-mantra for you.

By the power of the empowerment of this seal-mantra, visualize that nectar flows forth from within the seal, forming an ocean of milk that pours throughout the entire Dharma-realm to universally benefit you all."
All sentient beings are fully satisfied and satiated.
You karmic-obstruction spirits, though you may transform yourselves into fire, you cannot consume [this food]; now, by reciting these secret words, all shall be satiated with the Dharma-food.
Next, recite the mantra for the spirits who obstruct giving:
Oṃ āḥ hūṃ caṇḍā-miḍaṃ sarvā-pṛthag-vikṛte svāhā. (The mudrā and the dharani may be understood accordingly;
one should extend [the fingers] downward.)
Visualize the syllable *vaṃ* within the right palm.
From the bindu, nectar flows forth and descends from the left palm. Contemplate this.
Recite "Oṃ Āḥ Hrīḥ Hūṃ" one hundred and eight times, or twenty-one times as appropriate.
The attendant prostrates before the master, takes the pure flask, and exits the maṇḍala to fetch pure water.
Pour [the water] down slowly. When the Master reaches the point of chanting, he should imagine that the spirits obstructing the giving all kneel with their right knees on the ground.

The Master visualizes himself as Avalokiteśvara, appearing before each of them and bestowing nectar. It enters through the crown of their heads, extinguishing the fires of their karma so that they attain coolness.
Recite the mantra three times, snapping the fingers once after each recitation. Recite the mantra three or seven times for the spirits obstructing the giving.
Being thus fully satisfied and filled with joy, they snap their fingers once.

At that moment, the practitioner, holding the vessel of nectar in his right hand, stands facing east and pours it out before the altar, or upon clean ground, or upon a stone, or into a new, clean earthenware basin—also known as a *ūrṇa-patra* (or *bowl for the hungry ghosts*)—or even upon a raised platform;
or else into a spring, pond, river, sea, or flowing stream.
One must not pour [offerings] beneath pomegranate or peach trees, for the ghosts and spirits will be terrified; one must not eat from them.
If food and drink are offered to the assembly of noble ones, the Vidyārājas, or the various devas, they should be placed upon a living platform; this is the original method.
If making offerings to the Buddhas and the assembly of noble ones, the time for offering is at the fifth watch of the night, at dawn when the sun rises. As for the ghosts...

Regarding the deity ritual: at the fixed hour of *hai* (10–11 p.m. for humans, or at the practitioner's own fixed time, according to the method of the *ācārya*, if it is during the time of the fast, one may spend the entire day merely consecrating food, drink, water, and so forth, and bestowing them as offerings upon birds, wild animals, and aquatic creatures that fly through the air.

Do not select specific times; simply perform the offering as usual. However, if one performs the ritual for offering food to hungry ghosts (*preta*), it should be done during the hour of Hai (9–11 p.m.).
If one offers food to hungry ghosts during the time of the midday meal, it will be a mere waste of effort and will ultimately have no effect.

Offering at an improper time is a false and deceptive act; the spirits and ghosts will not receive the food. Not following the teacher’s instructions invites calamity upon oneself and leads to failure.
Regarding the offense of stealing the Dharma: The *Samantabhadra-maṇḍala-sūtra* states that snapping the fingers with the left hand causes all virtuous deeds to be swiftly accomplished.
The *Susiddhikara-sādhana-upāyika-paṭala* states that snapping the fingers with the right hand causes a swift assembly [of deities].
(The *Susiddhikara* also states that snapping the fingers with both hands is a method for expelling obstructive spirits.)
O Sons of the Buddhas, although beings are categorized by their kind and grouped by their nature, my giving is entirely without obstruction;
it is without high or low, equal and universal, making no distinction between enemy and kin.

On this day, you must not treat the humble with contempt because they are noble, nor oppress the weak because they are strong, nor obstruct the orphaned and young so that they do not receive food, thereby making the distribution unjust.
Transcending the Buddha’s compassionate aid, you must necessarily cherish one another, maintaining a thought like that of parents remembering their children. He said to the sons of the Buddha:
"Each of you has your own parents, brothers and sisters, wives and children, retinues, virtuous friends, and kinsmen."
Should there be those who, due to some circumstance, are unable to come, you, sons of the Buddha, should regard them with a heart of compassion and affection.
Each of you should bring food, drink, money, and goods to bestow upon one another in turn, so that they may be fully satisfied and lack for nothing.

Cause them to resolve their minds upon the Way, so that they may forever leave the three miserable realms behind, eternally transcend the four currents, cast off this physical body, and swiftly surpass to the fruits of the Path. Furthermore, for their sake—
"You all, take this pure food and divide it into three portions. First, give it to the aquatic creatures so that they may realize the emptiness of persons (*pudgala-śūnyatā*).

Second, give it to the furred animals so that they may attain the tranquility of phenomena (*dharma-śānti*). Third, give it to those in other regions who possess consciousness and mold their forms, ensuring they are all fully satisfied and attain the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*)."
Through the empowerment of divine mantras, purify the Dharma-food; May it be universally bestowed upon all spirits and deities as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
May they all be fully satiated, abandon stinginess and greed, Swiftly escape the dark realms, and be reborn in the Pure Land.
Next, form the seal of universal offering.
Oṃ kakkhaṭa-saṃbhava vajra hūṃ. (The hand seal and mantra may be understood as follows:
one should visualize the place where the middle fingers are bent, and visualize the white syllable Oṃ.)
From the syllables and bindus, inexhaustible offerings flow forth.
With complete adornment, perform the offering of equality.
Recite "Universal Offering" in unison.
Recite the mantra either five or seven times.
Question: Since the initial offering to the Triple Gem and the distribution of food have already been completed, why perform this offering again now?

Answer: What was performed previously involved distinguishing between the noble and the ordinary; therefore, after making offerings to the Triple Gem, one bestowed [offerings] upon the host of spirits.
Now, by integrating them through equality, the noble and the ordinary interpenetrate; this is why one makes universal offerings.

When the *Vina* has finished reciting the text for the food and drink received from the outset, the Master should perform the fivefold offering, bestow the precious *caṛuka*, and recite the *Smarā* mantras and others.
(The Ritual Manual of the Tathāgata Amitāyus states: Next, bind the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Mahākāśa. Join the two hands in *añjali*.
Cross the two middle fingers externally, with the right pressing over the left, so that they touch the backs of the hands. Bring the two index fingers together in the shape of a jewel.
One should then visualize that from within this mudrā flow forth immeasurable articles of offering, such as clothing, food, and drink.)

"O sons of the Buddhas, all the food and drink you have received from the past were obtained through the sale of living beings in the human world—money for wine and dried meats, blood and flesh, tainted by raw meat and stench, pungent and foul-smelling.

Although you have received such food and drink, it is like a poisonous medicine that damages the body, only increasing the wood of suffering and causing you to sink into the sea of misery with no time of liberation. I, now..."
In accordance with the Tathāgata’s teachings, with sincere devotion and complete self-sacrifice, this great and universal Dharma assembly has been established.
Today you have encountered this supreme occasion; the precepts have permeated your bodies, and in past lives you have extensively served various Buddhas and drawn near to virtuous friends.
